property_summary: For any caller and any _baseToken argument, after initialize(...) completes the contract's public baseToken equals the provided _baseToken; the mutant that stores msg.sender instead breaks this (baseToken != _baseToken) for inputs where msg.sender != _baseToken.

For any inputs to initialize, the deployed contract's baseToken equals the _baseToken argument passed (the reference preserves the caller's chosen base token), whereas the mutant that forces baseToken = address(0) will violate this for some inputs where _baseToken != address(0).

For any call to initialize(...), the contract's public baseToken equals the _baseToken argument passed (reference: baseToken is set to _baseToken); the mutant sets baseToken to royaltyRegistry instead and thus will violate this for inputs where _baseToken != royaltyRegistry.

After initialize(...) completes, the nft getter returns the same address as the _nft parameter passed in (reference satisfies for all inputs); the mutant that assigns nft = address(0) breaks this by returning zero instead of the provided _nft for some inputs.
For any initialize(...) call that succeeds, the contract's public nft() equals the _nft argument given; the mutant assigns nft to factory instead, so for some inputs nft() != _nft.

For any fuzzed _changeFee value passed to initialize, the contract's stored changeFee equals the provided _changeFee (no silent increment); the mutant that stores _changeFee + 1 will violate this for some inputs.

For any initialize(...) call on a fresh C, the contract's changeFee state equals the provided _changeFee; the mutant that forces changeFee=0 will violate this whenever _changeFee != 0 (some fuzzed inputs).

For any uint56 _changeFee, after initialize(...) completes the contract's public changeFee equals the exact _changeFee passed in (reference); the mutant stores a shifted/truncated value so for some fuzzed _changeFee the getter differs and the assertion fails.

After any call to initialize(...) by any caller with any admissible arguments, the reference contract always sets initialized to true and subsequent re-initialization attempts revert (i.e., the second initialize cannot succeed), whereas the mutant allows a second initialize call to succeed and thus changes state on the second call.

For all inputs where feeRate > 5000, the reference contract's initialize must revert (preventing initialized from becoming true), whereas the mutant removes this check and will allow initialization with feeRate > 5000, so initialized becomes true for some fuzzed inputs.

For every call to initialize(..., _payRoyalties) the contract's public payRoyalties getter equals the provided _payRoyalties; the mutant flips it (so for some fuzzed _payRoyalties the stored value differs).

For any initialize(...) call the reference contract sets useStolenNftOracle equal to the _useStolenNftOracle argument passed in; the mutant always sets useStolenNftOracle to false, so for some inputs (when _useStolenNftOracle == true) the mutant's post-initialize getter differs from the reference.

For any initialize(...) call, the reference implementation sets the stored useStolenNftOracle state to the boolean passed as _useStolenNftOracle; the mutant incorrectly always sets useStolenNftOracle to true, so there exist inputs where the stored value differs from the provided _useStolenNftOracle (specifically when _useStolenNftOracle == false).

For any inputs to initialize, the contract's virtualBaseTokenReserves equals the _virtualBaseTokenReserves argument after initialize completes; the mutant sets virtualBaseTokenReserves to _virtualNftReserves instead, so for inputs where _virtualBaseTokenReserves != _virtualNftReserves the mutant will violate this property.

For any inputs to initialize, the reference contract sets virtualBaseTokenReserves equal to the _virtualBaseTokenReserves argument (and virtualNftReserves equal to _virtualNftReserves); the mutant that swaps assignments can produce a mismatch where virtualBaseTokenReserves != the provided _virtualBaseTokenReserves.

After initialize(...) returns successfully, virtualBaseTokenReserves equals the provided _virtualBaseTokenReserves parameter for the reference implementation for all inputs; the mutant that sets virtualBaseTokenReserves to 0 breaks this invariant for inputs where _virtualBaseTokenReserves != 0.
